correctness.rationale: For two normalized independent planar rows, conjugation symmetry forces the averaged error Gram to be bisector-diagonal. Exact multiplication gives its sum and difference as the two displayed polynomials. Positive derivative of the first diagonal and the unique critical point of the second, followed by the monotone cubic crossover calculation, prove the full real-parameter unique minimax. The conditional recursion bound requires fresh independent epoch permutations only. The verifier reproduces symbolic identities and exact finite Gram calculations; proof provides all infinite quantifiers.

value.rationale: Gives the complete optimal common relaxation as a function of the natural row coherence for a uniformly reshuffled two-equation projection solver, with a nontrivial phase transition between equalizing directional risk and stationarity of its dominant direction. Strict optimal overrelaxation holds throughout the nonorthogonal planar regime, supplying a precise tuning benchmark; avoids claims about practical runtime or asymptotic rate.
